projects.title: Cloud-Intel
projects.subtitle: Proof-of-concept for the AWS cloud-attribution work (live)
projects.description: Built to automate what I was doing manually at AWS - identifying which VC-funded startups are running on which cloud and AI providers and prioritizing which ones to engage. A live AI intelligence platform tracking 200+ VC-funded startups with cloud and AI provider attribution, vertical classification, and engagement prioritization. Core: a 4-tier attribution engine (deterministic signals → strong inference → supporting signals → dual LLM fallback via Perplexity Sonar + Claude Haiku) with confidence scoring and entrenchment ratings. Scans DNS records, subprocessor/DPA pages, job postings across 15 VC job boards, partnership announcements, technical docs, privacy policies, IP/ASN ranges, and tech blogs - ~2,500 automated web searches per daily pipeline run. Phase 1 added vertical/sub-vertical classification across 84 sub-verticals with cloud propensity tags (High/Medium/Low). Phase 2 added engagement priority tiers (Engage Now / Watch / Track), trigger detection (hiring surges, leadership changes, product launches, press features, vendor partnerships), and LLM-generated outreach intelligence with a dedicated “Ready to Engage” view. Phase 3 added API cost observability - granular per-function search usage tracking with a stacked bar chart and KPI cards on the dashboard. Architected and shipped end to end with AI-assisted development (Claude Code).
projects.stack: FastAPI, Python, Next.js, Supabase, Claude API (Anthropic), Claude Code, Perplexity Sonar, Serper.dev (Google Search), Recharts, Railway, Vercel
projects.outcome: Live and reachable at cloud-intel.vercel.app (app and collected data browsable). When running, the daily pipeline tracks 167+ startups with cloud/AI attribution, vertical classification, propensity tags, engagement tiers, trigger detection, LLM-generated outreach intelligence, and API cost monitoring across 6 dashboard views. The proof-of-concept that informed my AWS cloud-attribution work; pipeline currently paused, restartable anytime.

professional_ai_projects.title: Executive Decision & Intelligence System - Startup Pulse
professional_ai_projects.description: Architected the multi-agent AI system behind Startup Pulse, a CEO-facing reporting program. Its job is synthesis, not collection: a coordinated agent pipeline gathers, consolidates, reviews, and formats, but the product of the system is derived analysis. It takes a broad view across external market signal (funding, hiring, product launches, trust pages, job postings) and internal first-party data (revenue, growth, CRM engagement, pipeline) and infers strategic metrics that exist in no source system, including Primary Cloud Provider and Primary AI Provider. Aggregating what is already recorded is a dashboard; deriving a number nobody reports is the hard part, and that is what this does. The output is a 360-degree view per startup: internal metrics, CRM engagement, external funding signals, customer snapshots, and cloud/AI provider inference. It tracks a self-refreshing set of 2000+ startups (every funded startup past a $30M bar or with a high-pedigree founding team, not a static list) and powers three CEO-facing reporting cadences: a monthly top-50 funded list, a quarterly top-1000, and a top-500 report for the Bi-Weekly Business Review (BWBR) reviewed by Andy Jassy and his direct reports.
professional_ai_projects.stack: Amazon Quick, PizzaBot, Salesforce MCP integration
professional_ai_projects.outcome: Reduced end-to-end report production from 6 weeks to under a week, a 70% reduction in report generation time, recovering 600 hours per cycle across three individuals and enabling consistent, scalable executive delivery without analyst bottlenecks. Cited by Andy Jassy in Amazon's Q4 2025 earnings call.

professional_ai_projects.title: PCP Reference App
professional_ai_projects.subtitle: Leadership Product - AI-inferred market metric
professional_ai_projects.description: A leadership-facing product that turned Primary Cloud Provider, a critical but previously unmeasurable metric, into something reliable and on-demand. Prior approaches (third-party usage data, wallet-share proxies) failed; about 2.5 years ago I pioneered a qualitative-plus-quantitative triangulation framework combining external signals (trust pages, job postings) with internal signals (Salesforce notes, revenue, growth, pipeline) to infer a startup's PCP and PAIP. I took it through three architectural generations, each answering a different product question. First, an external-search-only prototype that proved the metric was inferable at all, but with no internal data to check itself against it hallucinated confidently. Second, a version that brought external search and internal first-party data together with a model synthesizing the PCP call, which is where the product crossed from interesting to decision-grade: the validation layer did that, not the model. Third, a rebuild on Amazon Quick, which abstracts the plumbing and lets the product run without depending on one person. Originally a manual process capped at ~20 startups a month; with AI it scaled and the decision heuristic itself improved. Validated through 1,000+ seller conversations over two years, which functioned as the ground-truth loop: every seller disagreement was a labeled example of where the inference was wrong, and that feedback built the eval that converted output into evidence. It surfaces competitive context (including neocloud and GPU-provider usage) and feeds directly into startup strategy.

professional_ai_projects.outcome: Went from hallucinated output to decision-grade signal, and from fully manual effort to under 30%. Andy Jassy's office acted as the design partner, setting the accuracy bar the product had to clear, then reaching for it repeatedly in live reviews to direct where AWS acts, win back non-primary startups, trigger net-new account creation, and inform credit disbursement. professional_ai_projects.title: Proactive Intelligence Engine (Claude-side prototype)
professional_ai_projects.subtitle: Agentic System - dual build
professional_ai_projects.description: The frontier reference build of the Proactive Intelligence pillar, built on Claude to define the ideal state, then replicated within Amazon's internal tooling. A watcher (signal detection) feeds a classifier and an account-manager writer agent. Two systems give it memory and self-correction. For memory, I integrated GBrain, an open-source knowledge-graph store, writing the Python adapter that bridges it to the pipeline: each net-new signal becomes a page with a typed edge to its company page, recall is a hybrid vector and keyword query run before generation, and a semantic dedup pass catches reworded restatements of the same event rather than only exact-string matches, so briefs lead with what actually changed. I designed the memory layer behind a backend-agnostic seam, so the real GBrain store and a self-written Supabase fallback are interchangeable. For quality, I wrote Hermes, a self-improving skill loop that scores every brief with a structured critique and aggregates critiques across runs into a proposed revision of the writer's style guide. Hermes is propose-only by design: it never edits a live skill file, so a human reviews and approves each change and the loop stays auditable rather than autonomous. Its automated scores are calibrated against human account-manager ratings captured through a lightweight CLI. Two rejection paths keep bad output from reaching a reader: classifier confidence below threshold routes a signal to a review queue instead of the writer, and when memory reports zero net-new signals the pipeline returns no_change and skips the brief entirely, spending nothing rather than producing filler. Quality changes are verified by a frozen-fixture eval harness that replays inputs at temperature zero and judges pairwise with bidirectional consistency, so a winner must win both orderings or the result is scored a tie, which cancels position bias. Runs on Claude Code, designed to migrate to Bedrock AgentCore.
professional_ai_projects.stack: Claude (Sonnet + Haiku), Perplexity Sonar, GBrain (open-source knowledge-graph memory, PGLite store) integrated via a self-written Python adapter, Hermes (self-authored skill-scoring loop), Supabase, frozen-fixture eval harness
professional_ai_projects.outcome: A memory and feedback architecture that lets an AI-generated intelligence pipeline avoid redundant output and continuously calibrate its own writing quality against human judgment, without hand-tuning prompts for every iteration. Also a working frontier prototype that maps what the evolving model frontier enables, then transfers those patterns into Amazon's constrained tooling to maximize value for leadership stakeholders.

professional_ai_projects.title: PCP-Intel: Attribution Accuracy Auto-Optimization Loop
professional_ai_projects.subtitle: Agentic System - In Design
professional_ai_projects.description: Designed to eliminate manual signal weight tuning in the Cloud-Intel cloud attribution pipeline - replacing ad-hoc threshold adjustments with an autonomous overnight optimization loop modeled on Karpathy's AutoResearch pattern. A validation agent runs the attribution pipeline against a curated, human-verified ground truth eval set of 30-50 startups stratified across confidence tiers, PCP categories, and known edge cases (multi-cloud, conflicting signals, false positive-prone patterns). An optimization agent reads the current signal weight config and a natural-language research brief, forms a hypothesis, proposes a targeted weight adjustment across five attribution signals (partnership pages, subprocessor lists, DNS records, marketplace listings, job postings), and re-scores against a composite accuracy metric that penalizes false positives more heavily than misses. A logging agent persists each experiment - hypothesis, config delta, score delta, keep/revert decision - to Supabase, building an auditable history of what the pipeline learned. Runs ~12 experiments per hour unattended, surfacing the best-performing config each morning.
professional_ai_projects.stack: Claude (multi-agent orchestration), MCP (Supabase, Filesystem), Brave Search
professional_ai_projects.outcome: Designed to replace manual attribution tuning with a closed-loop, evidence-driven optimization system - continuously improving PCP signal accuracy overnight and surfacing a validated, experiment-backed config ready for production promotion each morning.
